recipes.name: Uli's Apple Red Cabbage
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup red wine, or to taste
2 tablespoons apple cider vinegar, or to taste
2 teaspoons white sugar, or to taste
0.25 teaspoon ground nutmeg, or to taste
1 pinch ground cinnamon, or to taste
salt and ground pepper to taste

steps.text: Melt butter in a stockpot over medium-high heat. Stir in bacon and cook until just beginning to crisp, 4 to 6 minutes. Add onions; cook and stir until onions are lightly browned and translucent, 6 to 8 minutes.

Stir in chicken broth, red wine, apple slices, and apple cider vinegar; bring to a boil. Stir in sugar, cloves, bay leaves, nutmeg, cinnamon, salt, and black pepper. Stir in red cabbage; cover, reduce heat to low, and simmer until cabbage is soft and cooked through, 30 to 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Uli's Apple Red Cabbage
raw_recipe.description: My grandmother was a master housewife. She taught home economics and she could cook. When she cooked this apple red cabbage my brother and I would eat it hot or cold, with or without potatoes!

review.reviewBody: This is Authentic and Awesome! My parents emigrated from Germany in 1955 and I grew up with my Mothers version of this same recipe. Don’t be surprised if it takes a bit longer to soften up. Mine usually takes about one and a quarter hours on a low simmer. Sehr gut. Machen Sie es!

Basically followed the recipe, but did not use butter, and substituted soy bacon for real bacon. Put all ingredients in the crock pot and cooked on high for 2 hours and then on low for 3 hours. Could have cooked on high longer. Also added a boullion cube and more spices. Calories came to 157 per serving.
This is good as is but after making this several times I double the bacon and onion and omit the cloves. Also I have found that dicing the apples works better than slices. Thanks for the recipe!

I'll be honest...my rating likely has more to do with my personal preferences than any reflection on the recipe or chef. I'm just not a huge fan of cooked cabbage. That said, it was a nice side dish to compliment the Schnitzel and Spaetzle I had already prepared. I would probably make it again under the same circumstances, but not on its own. I would also likely increase the vinegar and perhaps add some mustard or horseradish to zing it up a bit.

My first time making Rotkohl from scratch. It’s hard to find German-style red cabbage in GB, so I used this recipe. My husband is German, and he asked me to leave out the bacon, which I did. Otherwise, I followed the recipe. He said the spices were on point, but it needed to be a little fruitier. He added a wee bit more vinegar and sugar, then apple juice and orange juice. The flavor is milder than a jar brand like Hengstenberg, but personally, we all preferred this recipe.

Great recipe, very authentic. I like to take a whole small onion and stick the cloves in the onion. You will have the flavor of both without having to fish for the cloves to remove them when finished cooking. Sehr lecker!!

I am also from Germany and was looking for a good and authentic recipe. This is it! I didn't have red wine so I added a couple TBSP red wine vinegar. I also cut sugar in half and this still came out delicious! My sister raved about it also. Can't wait to pick up some red wine and make again! A keeper for sure! Einfach Wunderbar!
Great recipe my family loved it. I let it set up in refrigerator for 48hrs, reheated on low until bubbling, was awesome.

This is the way my mother taught me to make red cabbage! It is a perfect side dish to pork chops and mashed potatoes, to goulash, and many other German dishes. Make a big batch and freeze some to pull out for a quick side dish when you’re pressed for time.
I Enjoyed this! Perfect as written.
I've made this several times and it delicious. The only change I made was that I used 3 large very tart apples and cider vinegar ... made to my taste. Thank you for sharing.
We used your recipe as inspiration to create our own Blaukraut recipe. It was our first attempt. It turned out amazing!! Thank you for sharing your recipe.
No changes. Even better left over.
Excellent!!!! Couldn’t help snacking on it all day long!!!!

Wunderbar! Made this exactly per directions, except I halved the recipe. Made it the day before I served it. Took almost 90 minutes for cabbage to get tender (despite the fact that I shredded it very finely). Well worth the wait, and a day in the fridge allowed all of the flavors to meld. Served it with spaetzle and rouladen. It doesn’t get any better than this if you like German food!
This was wonderful,especially with the apple slices and the spicees,even picky husband lovd it!Thankyou Grama Uli!

A wonderful side dish. I made it to go with pork chops and my husband and I loved it. It had just the right amount of tang and sweetness. It was easy to put together while I was preparing other foods. My only negative comment would be that while the recipe says that it serves four, it would easily serve 6-8 people. We both had very generous servings and I have way more than half of it left. Next time I will halve the recipe—unless I want some for another day.
